property_summary: The supportsInterface function returns true for an interface ID that is either IAccessControl or IERC165, but not both.
After canceling a scheduled operation with ID id, the timestamp for that operation should be 0 (not pending or ready or done).
The supportsInterface function returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID when called on a timelock that has had an operation canceled.
The supportsInterface function returns false for the IERC165 interface ID when called before any operation is scheduled.
supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl interface ID after calling cancel with an operation ID that is pending
For any role bytes32, hasRole(role, address(0)) must return the same as supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) already being true.
For any bytes32 id, if cancel(id) succeeds without reverting, then c.hasRole(c.TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE(), msg.sender) must be true.
For any address account, supportsInterface returns true if account has the IAccessControl role, and cancel never reverts for a pending operation only when the caller is the proposer.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, calling supportsInterface returns true when interfaceId equals IAccessControl interfaceId, regardless of the state of cancel operations.
supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) must return true when cancel is never called
For any bytes4 interfaceId, calling supportsInterface should return true if and only if the interfaceId matches IAccessControl or IERC165.
Calling supportsInterface with type(IERC165).interfaceId should return true on the reference contract but false on the mutant.
After any cancel operation, calling supportsInterface with the ERC165 interface ID returns true.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, calling supportsInterface returns true if and only if interfaceId matches IAccessControl or IERC165.
The supportsInterface function returns true for the ERC165 interface ID after any cancel operation.
For any interface ID, supportsInterface returns true if and only if it matches IAccessControl (0x7965db0b) or the ERC165 base supports it.
For any ID, supportsInterface returns the same result before and after a cancel call.
supportsInterface returns correct values consistently across different interface IDs
The supportsInterface function never returns true for both the IAccessControl interface ID and a different interface ID when called with the same interface ID.
The supportsInterface function returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID (0x7965db0b) before and after a cancel operation.
For a given operation ID, the cancel function should revert when the operation is not pending, regardless of who calls it.
cancel(bytes32) should keep the operation timestamp unchanged when called by an address without PROPOSER_ROLE.
The function cancel(bytes32) should revert if the caller does not have PROPOSER_ROLE and the caller is not the contract itself.
cancel(bytes32) should revert when called by an address without PROPOSER_ROLE, regardless of whether the operation is pending.
cancel(bytes32) should revert when called by an address that does not have PROPOSER_ROLE and is not the contract itself.
After any cancel call, the getRoleAdmin for the PROPOSER_ROLE should always return TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE (the admin role set in constructor), but the bug hardcodes 0x00.

After constructing C with the specified admin roles, calling getRoleAdmin on any role that was explicitly assigned an admin role in the constructor should return the TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE (keccak256("TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE")) and not the constant DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00).
After cancellation of an operation, the admin role of PROPOSER_ROLE remains TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE (non-zero) and not the hardcoded 0x00.
Calling getRoleAdmin on any role assigned an admin role in the constructor returns a non-zero value.
getRoleAdmin(PROPOSER_ROLE) == TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE after constructor for any fuzzed role
After calling cancel with any id, the role renounceRole never succeeds for the caller (reverts).
After calling cancel with any id, the TimelockController still allows the caller to renounce its PROPOSER_ROLE.
After calling cancel with any id, the caller can still renounce its PROPOSER_ROLE if it has it.
After calling cancel on any operation, the PROPOSER_ROLE of the caller is not affected (i.e., they can still renounce it).
After canceling an operation, the caller can still renounce their PROPOSER_ROLE.
For any bytes32 id, calling cancel(id) should revert if isOperation(id) returns false, or succeed if isOperation(id) returns true and the caller has the PROPOSER_ROLE.
For any bytes32 id, if cancel(id) does not revert, then isOperation(id) should still return true after the cancel call.
For any bytes32 id, cancel(id) should revert if isOperation(id) returns false (i.e., the operation is not pending).
Calling cancel on an operation id should revert if isOperation(id) returns false before the call.
For any bytes32 id, isOperation(id) should return the same value before and after calling cancel(id) if the cancel would revert.
For any bytes32 id, calling cancel with a non-pending operation reverts before the mutant can falsely accept it.
After a successful schedule, calling cancel with the operation id does not revert.
For a successfully scheduled operation, cancel reverts when called after the operation is executed via the timelock.
Calling cancel on an operation that has been executed (isOperationDone returns true) reverts.
Calling cancel on an operation that has not been scheduled (isOperation returns false) must revert.
For any scheduled operation, isOperationPending returns true only after the operation is scheduled and before it is executed.
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) is greater than isOperationDone(id) in the reference contract.
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) and isOperationDone(id) cannot both be true simultaneously.
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) returns false when the timestamp is exactly _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) returns true if and only if getTimestamp(id) > _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
A scheduled operation must always be pending (i.e., isOperationPending returns true) until it is explicitly cancelled.
A cancelled operation must immediately have isOperationPending return false.
For any id, after a successful cancel, isOperationPending(id) must be false.
Before any operation is scheduled, isOperationPending returns false for any id.
If isOperationPending returns false for an id, then isOperationDone must return true for that id.
If an operation is scheduled, cancel succeeds; otherwise cancel reverts.
Cancelling an operation returns true (does not revert) if and only if the operation is pending (isOperationPending returns true).
isOperationPending returns true if and only if cancel does not revert for that operation id
cancel(id) succeeds (does not revert) if and only if isOperationPending(id) returns true.
If cancel(id) does not revert, then isOperationPending(id) must have returned true before that call.
After canceling an operation, it is no longer pending (isOperationPending returns false).
Before canceling a pending operation, the operation is pending (isOperationPending returns true).
After canceling a pending operation, isOperationPending returns false for that operation.
An operation that is not scheduled (isOperationPending returns false) cannot be canceled (cancel reverts).
If an operation is pending (isOperationPending returns true) then after calling cancel(id) the operation is done (isOperationDone returns true).
If cancel(id) succeeds (does not revert), then after the call, isOperationDone(id) must return true for that id.
If an operation is not pending (isOperationPending returns false), then calling cancel(id) must revert.

If an operation is ready (isOperationReady returns true), then cancel(id) should revert before the operation can be executed; if cancel does not revert, isOperationDone must return true after the call.
After a successful cancel(id), isOperationDone(id) should return true for that id.
cancel reverts if the operation is not pending; otherwise it succeeds and makes the operation not pending.
After a schedule and execute with the required roles, the timestamp of the operation is 1 (done) and cancel reverts because the operation is no longer pending.
After cancel successfully completes, the operation timestamp remains unchanged (still zero) if the operation was not pending.
The timestamp returned by getTimestamp for a given operation id is constant over time and only changes when the operation is scheduled or executed.
After a cancel call returns without revert, isOperationPending for the canceled id returns false.
For any operation id, the timestamp returned by getTimestamp after cancel() is either 0 or _DONE_TIMESTAMP, not equal to block.timestamp.
After cancel(), the timestamp for the cancelled operation must be 0 (operation no longer pending), not equal to block.timestamp.
After scheduling and then cancelling an operation, the operation's timestamp must be 0 (not pending), not identical to block.timestamp.
After cancel() is called on a pending operation, getTimestamp(id) must return 0, which is not equal to block.timestamp (the buggy return value).
The timestamp of a canceled operation must be 0, not block.timestamp.
After cancel is called, the timestamp of the operation becomes _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
getTimestamp for a canceled operation returns _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) if the operation was pending before cancel.
After a successful cancel, the operation's timestamp equals _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) if it was pending before the cancel call.
For any operation that is pending, calling cancel makes getTimestamp return _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
For any operation id, getTimestamp should not return _DONE_TIMESTAMP for an unscheduled operation, but the buggy version does.
For any bytes32 id, if isOperationPending(id) is false, then isOperationDone(id) must be false.
For any bytes32 id, isOperation(id) must imply isOperationPending(id).
For any bytes32 id, if isOperationPending(id) is true, then cancel(id) must succeed (not revert).

For any bytes32 id, getTimestamp(id) must return a value that is sufficient to determine isOperationPending: if getTimestamp(id) > 1 then isOperationPending must be true, and if getTimestamp(id) <= 1 then isOperationPending must be false.
For any bytes32 id, cancel(id) reverts exactly when isOperationPending(id) returns false.
